snippet.text: `lensPolicyHook` runs before every tool call in a conversation that has a `LensDocument`, and passes every other call untouched. It blocks a tool the lens did not list, a severity outside its `severities`, and a rule outside its `rules`, listing the rules that exist. A `melian/other-defect` finding passes the rule check because the review appended the rule, and keeps to the lens's severities. The one exception to the severities is an injection attempt at P1: the injection policy orders every lens to report one at P1, so `conventions`, which declares P2 and P3, can still do so; an injection attempt at any other severity is bounded like any finding. The model reads the reason as the tool result and can correct itself.

snippet.text: The verifier also lowers, by the same one step, a finding rated above what its own scenario costs on the lenses' severity scale, such as a missing test or a wrong document reported at P1, as [the decision of 2026-11-28](decisions/2026-11-28-lenses-report-every-real-defect.md) sets out. A document that describes a behaviour never refutes a claim that the behaviour breaks something that reads it; the verifier judges the outcome the claim names.

snippet.text: Builder agent, for [issue #655](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/issues/655). Six built-in lenses, `contracts`, `correctness`, `design`, `removed-behaviour`, `tests` and `trust-boundary`, now review as the review of record does. Each first learns what the change promises, then attacks each promise, and reports every real defect it meets: under its own rules, or under the new `melian/other-defect`, which the review adds to every lens beside `melian/injection-attempt`. Hand-offs describe a neighbour's focus, and no longer tell a lens to leave a defect to it. The shared instructions in `packages/core/src/lens.ts` add one severity scale, read by what happens once the change is merged. The verifier may lower by one step a finding its own scenario does not support, and a document that describes a behaviour no longer refutes a claim that the behaviour breaks something. The coordinator's uncommitted experiment, on five merged pull requests, raised the share of reviewers' defects Melian found from 35% to 50% at the same count of blocking findings; [the decision](../decisions/2026-11-28-lenses-report-every-real-defect.md) records the numbers. Applying the experiment's diff to today's `main` kept the lens rules it had dropped by accident, those that were not hold-back sentences: `contracts` reporting the broken dependant's location, `design`'s author standard and report-once rule, `tests`' fake and untested-module rules, and `trust-boundary`'s supply-chain sentence. No findings budget, route, tier or level changed. No key changed shape. Lens versions, the verifier's version and the request keys moved with their text, so the first round after this lands asks every lens and the verifier again once.

snippet.text: - `handoffs` maps a neighbouring lens's name to the defects it owns. The lens's instructions list them, to leave to that neighbour, only in a review that runs the neighbour. Problem: `contracts`, `trust-boundary`, `removed-behaviour`, and `tests` run only in the `full` tier, and the `pre-push` and `comment` stages run `standard`, which holds `correctness` alone. Example: a `correctness` told unconditionally that a deleted cleanup belongs to `removed-behaviour`, or a broken caller to `contracts`, passes a `pre-push` review that deletes one or breaks one, since nothing else is looking. Solution: a hand-off is rendered from the review's selection, so a lens running without its neighbour keeps the coverage it had before the neighbour existed. It holds per file, for the files the neighbour covers among the lens's own: a `melian.yaml` that narrows `trust-boundary` to `src/server/**` would otherwise have `correctness` leave a shell injection in `src/cli/` to a lens that never reads it. When the neighbour covers some of the lens's files, the instructions name the neighbour, the defects it owns, and those files, and describe that lens's focus there; since [the decision of 2026-11-28](../decisions/2026-11-28-lenses-report-every-real-defect.md) they no longer tell the lens to leave a defect to it, and a lens reports every real defect it meets, under `melian/other-defect` when none of its own rules fits; when it covers every file, they say so without a list; when it covers none, no hand-off renders. A renamed file counts as one file: a neighbour selected through its old path covers its head path, as it does for its own findings, and one that covers its head path covers its old path. The files come from the change, so they reach the instructions inside the review's boundary for the change's data. A list holds at most 40 files and 4 KiB: past either, the hand-off to that neighbour is left out, and the lens's check record says so, so an author cannot grow a system prompt without bound by touching many files under [cut at 2 KiB]

snippet.text: A lens reviews as the review of record does. It first learns what the change promises, from the guidelines, decisions and tests the change touches, then attacks each promise. It reports every real defect it meets, whichever lens would own it: under one of its own rules when one fits, and otherwise under `melian/other-defect`, a rule Melian defines for every lens beside `melian/injection-attempt`. It reports a suspicion it could not trace to its end too, saying which step it could not trace, and leaves the proof to the verifier. Hand-offs describe each neighbour's focus and no longer tell a lens to leave a defect to it. Every lens rates a finding on one severity scale, by what happens once the change is merged: P0 loses or corrupts stored data, leaks a secret or runs an outside party's code in ordinary use; P1 makes merged code lose data, expose what it must protect, approve what it must refuse, or stop working; P2 is a narrower real wrong result, or a missing test for a guard on trust or stored data; P3 is any other missing test, a wrong message or document, a case that fails safely, or a design concern. [the decision of 2026-11-28](decisions/2026-11-28-lenses-report-every-real-defect.md) records why: on five merged pull requests the rewrite raised the share of reviewers' defects Melian found from 35% to 50%, and the scale kept blocking findings where `main` had them.
